name: Shenzhen Megmeet Electrical Co., Ltd. (深圳麦格米特电气股份有限公司)
summary: Megmeet is a power-electronics and electrical-automation company organized into six business groups: smart home appliance electric controls, power products (including AI data-center power), new energy vehicle & rail transit components, industrial automation, intelligent equipment (welding, industrial microwave, oil equipment), and precision connection. FY2025 revenue was ¥9.40B (+15.1%), roughly 40% of it overseas, with 10 R&D centers and 8 manufacturing bases across China, Thailand, India, the US, and Germany. Founded by Huawei Electric and Emerson Network Power alumni, it listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in 2017 and filed for a Hong Kong A+H dual listing in June 2026.
ecosystemRole: Megmeet sits in the ecosystem as a power-conversion supplier moving aggressively into AI data-center power: it is a member of NVIDIA's 800V HVDC ecosystem (the only mainland-China power vendor NVIDIA named for GB200 NVL72 power), building the grid-to-GPU chain — solid-state transformers, 800VDC sidecar cabinets, power/BBU/supercapacitor shelves, and server PSUs — that adjoins BESS players on the 'compute-power coordination' side. It also supplies PV/storage/EV-charging core components and storage PCS-adjacent power electronics.

productsAndServices.name: Power Products — AI Data-Center & Network Power
productsAndServices.description: Server/data-center power (CRPS/M-CRPS PSUs, power shelves, BBU and supercapacitor backup shelves, 800VDC sidecar cabinets, solid-state transformers), telecom/network power, medical power, industrial PSUs, LED/display power, and PV/storage/EV-charging core components. In 2025 the storage/charging high-voltage unit merged with network energy into a High-Efficiency Power business unit spanning data-center and storage high-voltage conversion.
highlights: Named by NVIDIA (Oct 2024) as a GB200 NVL72 power vendor — the only mainland-China power supplier on the list; member of NVIDIA's May 2025 800V HVDC ecosystem alliance
Full grid-to-GPU stack: AC compensator → BESS/backup shelves → SST (>98.5% efficiency, 800VDC out) → 1MW+ sidecar → 33kW/110kW power shelves → CRPS/M-CRPS/Power Brick point-of-load
Named network-power customers include Ericsson, Cisco, Juniper, Arista, Accton; batch deliveries of custom server power began end-2025
AI-DC revenue was NOT yet material in FY2025 (company's own characterization) — most projects pre-mass-production; first domestic hyperscaler volume delivery expected 2026
Dallas, Texas AI-DC power test lab opened Jun 2026 (360kW active capacity, 1.5MW roadmap)
productsAndServices.positioning: Claims to be one of the few mainland-China vendors combining high-power data-center power technology with overseas full-process production. Chasing a market ~74% held by Taiwanese suppliers (Delta ~41%, plus Lite-On, AcBel, Chicony, Advanced Energy); trade press reports Megmeet displacing Lite-On as the #2 NVIDIA power-shelf source behind Delta — market speculation, not company-confirmed.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct/ODM design-ins with server OEMs, cloud providers, and the NVIDIA reference ecosystem; network power sold direct to telecom/networking OEMs
productsAndServices.targetSegments: AI data centers (NVIDIA-architecture and domestic hyperscalers), telecom/networking OEMs, medical devices, industrial equipment
productsAndServices.roadmap: 800VDC architecture productization for NVIDIA Kyber/Vera Rubin-class racks (110kW liquid-cooled shelf shown May 2026); Dallas lab expansion to 1.5MW; first domestic hyperscaler volume delivery expected 2026; industry 1MW-rack adoption projected from 2027

strategyRead: Megmeet is running a classic incumbent-funded pivot: the mature appliance-controls business (38% of revenue, declining) and diversified industrial lines bankroll an all-in push on AI data-center power — R&D has held near 11–12% of revenue for a decade and FY2025 profit was deliberately sacrificed (ex-non-recurring profit −93%) to buy position in NVIDIA's 800VDC architecture transition.

Its wedge into the Delta-dominated (~41% share) server-power market is architecture timing, not price: it moved first among mainland vendors on the 800VDC sidecar/SST full-chain and is the only mainland supplier NVIDIA named for GB200 power — betting that the AC→800VDC transition (Kyber/Rubin, 1MW racks from ~2027) reshuffles supplier share before incumbents consolidate it.

The geographic build-out (Thailand phase II, Dallas test lab, India localization, HK listing) reads as supply-chain de-risking aimed at US hyperscaler procurement — a mainland company packaging itself to be buyable by American AI infrastructure buyers despite tariff and geopolitical friction.

Expectations are dangerously front-loaded relative to disclosure: the company itself said AI orders were immaterial through 2025, yet FY2026 consensus embeds a ~6x profit rebound — the Aug 27, 2026 H1 report is the first hard test of whether AI-DC power revenue actually materialized at scale.

The EV/rail segment doubling at 15% gross margin suggests a volume-share land-grab in commoditizing auto power electronics — strategically consistent (same power-electronics platform) but a drag on mix; the quiet margin engines are welding/intelligent equipment (38.5% GM) and industrial automation (28% GM).
